================================================================================
1. OBJECTIVES AND CONTEXT
================================================================================

[10:02]

IV: Morning both. Rowan, can you set the scene for us?

RE: We run field maintenance for about ninety thousand domestic connections.
The problem is visibility. When a customer rings to ask where their engineer
is, we have no line of sight at all and it's the single biggest driver of
complaints.

KP: My team takes around four hundred calls a week and I'd estimate half of
those are pure status chasing. It's a genuine concern for us because we've
been adding headcount every year.

IV: Is that measured or is it a feel?

KP: It's a feel, but we did tag call reasons for a fortnight last autumn and
status came out at fifty-one per cent. I can send that over.

[ACTION: KP to send the call-reason tagging analysis from autumn 2025]

RE: The board approved this on the basis of two measures. First-time fix above
eighty per cent, and no growth in service desk headcount.

================================================================================
2. REQUIREMENTS BY AREA
================================================================================

[10:24]

--- 2.1 JOB SCHEDULING ---

IV: What does good look like for scheduling?

RE: I want a scheduler to see every open job with its promised date, and I want
to be able to move work between engineers by dragging it. It has to be a human
making that call, not the system.

IV: So assisted scheduling rather than automatic.

RE: Yes. I've seen automatic scheduling and it was a disaster because it does
not know which engineers can work on which assets.

KP: Competency needs to be live data, not the spreadsheet the training team
keeps. That's non-negotiable if we are going to enforce it.

--- 2.2 CUSTOMER NOTIFICATIONS ---

KP: Ideally customers would get a message when the job is booked and another
when the engineer is on the way.

RE: I'd like that, but I accept it might be a phase two.

[PARKED: sequencing of customer notifications against the engineer mobile app]

================================================================================
3. CONSTRAINTS AND NEXT STEPS
================================================================================

[11:42]

RE: The billing system stays. It was replaced last year and nobody has the
appetite to touch it, so whatever we do has to integrate with it.

KP: And the engineers are offline for most of a working day. Roughly a third of
our sites have no usable data connection, so offline capture is mandatory.

IV: That's a significant technical requirement and I want to flag it as one of
the bigger risk areas. We'll pick it up in the technical session.

RE: We have never properly tested our disaster recovery, which I am saying out
loud so it is in the transcript.
